subject: Order Form security exhibit — escrow, inspection windows, and ephemeral pen-test access
messages:
From: Tom Martinez <tom@brightbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Sun <rebecca@legal.brightbridge.com>, Brightbridge Labs Security <security@brightbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Security exhibit redlines and operational asks (SOC 2 + pen test)

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft order form and security exhibit. Rebecca and our security team reviewed and attached a redline (Brightbridge_Redlines_v3.docx). A few of the high-level asks we want to clarify before legal will sign: 

- Inspection vs. audit language: we prefer explicit "inspection" wording and a limited scope (sampling) rather than open-ended audit rights.
- Pen test: define the window, access method (ephemeral credentials vs. VPN), and escalation procedure if an active vulnerability is found.
- SOC 2: We'll need the latest SOC 2 Type II (or an asserted control matrix) and a mapping of how Redwood's controls map to our requirements.
- Evidence cadence: how will logs and evidence be shared? Weekly bundles? On-demand ticketing?
- Escrow/forensic artifacts: do you support an escrowed snapshot or a pull-based evidence delivery?

Can you propose specific language and an operational runbook we can agree on? We're trying to avoid open-ended "inspection rights" that create production access without strict guards.

I've attached the redline and flagged some clauses. Happy to take a quick 30-min call to align.

Thanks,
Tom Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Brightbridge Labs

Attachments: Brightbridge_Redlines_v3.docx

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Martinez <tom@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and operational asks (SOC 2 + pen test)

Tom — thanks for the redline and the clear list. We can definitely tighten language and propose an operational pattern that limits exposure while giving Brightbridge the assurances you need. Proposed short plan below (happy to iterate on language):

1) Inspection language: change "audit rights" to "limited inspection rights". Inspections are limited to sampled artifacts and read-only access to logs and snapshots; no broad live-production access permitted. We'll add a clause requiring 30 days' notice for any privileged access requests.

2) Pen-test windows: propose a 3-week rolling window (client picks a 5-business-day testing slot within that window). All pen tests run against a staging environment unless a documented business exception is approved. For any production-facing tests, we require a five-step escalation and supervised session (see runbook link below).

3) Ephemeral access: technical approach is short-lived STS tokens or ephemeral SSH certs (max 8 hours), scoped to specific hosts and actions. Keys must be auto-revoked within 24 hours of test completion.

4) Evidence cadence: weekly evidence bundles (logs, alerts, changed config snapshots) for the duration of the testing window, plus a final consolidated report. For ad-hoc requests we can provide a ticketed on-demand export (SLA: 3 business days).

5) Escrow & artifacts: we recommend a pull-based escrow — we publish a signed, time-stamped snapshot into a secure customer-only bucket (retention 90 days) that Brightbridge can download. We can also support a third-party escrow on request.

I'll attach our SOC 2 assertion and propose exact wording for the exhibit in a follow-up. Can we do a 30-min sync next Wednesday 8/20 at 10:00 PT?

— Priyom
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Martinez <tom@brightbridge.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Sun <rebecca@legal.brightbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and operational asks (SOC 2 + pen test)

Tom / Priyom — a few legal redline suggestions to make the contract executable and aligned with our standard risk posture: 

- Replace the broad phrase "audit, inspection and access rights" with "limited inspection rights (as defined below)" and include a definition section that explains sampling, purpose, and acceptable methods.
- Limit inspection duration: any on-site or interactive inspection is limited to 48 consecutive hours except by mutual written agreement.
- Notice & privileged access: require at least 30 days' notice for privileged or interactive access; emergency exception language can be gated through an on-call SOC channel and must be expressly authorized by both parties' security leads.
- Scope: pen tests are scoped to a named environment and specific test cases; we will not allow unscripted lateral movement testing against production without technical and legal pre-approval.
- Evidence delivery: change "as requested" to a concrete cadence (weekly for testing periods; otherwise on request with a 3-business-day turnaround).

Karthik — can you confirm that the ephemeral access model Priyom proposed is technically feasible and whether the 48-hour interactive window is workable? I will draft a short exhibit insert and share redline language by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Martinez <tom@brightbridge.com>, Brightbridge Labs Security <security@brightbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 07:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and operational asks (SOC 2 + pen test)

Laura / Priyom / Tom — quick technical confirmation and a few implementation notes: 

- Ephemeral credentials: we can provision short-lived STS tokens with scoped IAM roles (max 8-hour lifetime) and session-specific logging. Tokens are audited and auto-rotated. We also support ephemeral SSH certificates via our certificate authority for limited shell access; certs expire automatically.

- Staging-only tests: strongly recommend running pen-tests against a production-like staging cluster. We can provide sanitized datasets and network-level parity. If you require production testing, we require a supervised session and we will only allow agentless checks (no interactive lateral movement).

- Evidence & escrow: we can generate signed snapshots (config, relevant logs, alert exports) on a per-test basis. Snapshot cadence: initial kickoff snapshot, then weekly snapshots during testing, and a final snapshot + aggregated logs at termination. Snapshots are written to a customer-only S3 bucket with presigned download links; we can also push to a third-party escrow on request.

- Forensics & escalation: if a critical finding is discovered we will initiate an emergency incident-runbook: containment steps, temporary elevated access (timeboxed to a maximum of 24 hours), and a joint post-mortem within 5 business days.

I'll attach the SOC2 artifact in the sync thread for your review (SOC2-report-2024.pdf). From an engineering standpoint, everything Priyom proposed is feasible. The main ask: legal should sign off on the 30-day notice requirement and the 48-hour interactive cap.

— Karthik
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-report-2024.pdf

From: Tom Martinez <tom@brightbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Sun <rebecca@legal.brightbridge.com>, Brightbridge Labs Security <security@brightbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit redlines and operational asks (SOC 2 + pen test)

Thanks — this is helpful and addresses most of our concerns. Rebecca and our security team reviewed Karthik's notes and are comfortable with the ephemeral token model and weekly snapshots. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize redlines: 

1) Exception for urgent production checks: we still want an emergency exception clause that allows a supervised, one-off production-facing test (strictly monitored and jointly authored checklist). Can we add a 24-hour supervised session with recorded screens and two-party approval?

2) Evidence retention: we prefer a 180-day retention for escrowed snapshots (instead of 90) for a rolling investigation window. Is that negotiable?

If you can incorporate these two items into the exhibit and send a marked-up order form by Friday EOD, legal will route for signature. We'll plan to take the 8/20 sync as scheduled to walk the runbook.

Best,
Tom Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Brightbridge Labs
